chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Isma'il ibn Abd al-Khaliq said:
I heard him saying: 'It is not appropriate for the Imam to stand up when he has prayed until everyone behind him has completed what was missed of the prayer.'

key_terms.يَقُومَ: To stand up (from sitting or bowing)
key_terms.يَقْضِيَ: To complete (a missed act of worship)

ai.seo_question: When should the Imam stand up to end the prayer if followers are catching up?
ai.summary: This ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Imam’s duty of *ta'abbud* (attentiveness) to the congregation, ensuring no follower is left in a state of incomplete prayer. It reflects the Shia emphasis on the Imam’s role as a shepherd who waits for the last follower, reinforcing the communal unity and legal precision of congregational worship.
